before.title: AIRMATIC Air Suspension Clunks and Premature Rear Shock/Damper Wear
before.description: EQS owners report low-speed clunking over bumps, uneven ride height, and a ride quality that drifts from floaty to harsh as mileage builds, traced to the AIRMATIC air-suspension system (worn sway-bar links, bushings, air struts, or compressor/valve-block degradation). On EQS SUVs in particular, premature rear shock-absorber/damper replacement has been documented, often within the first one to two years, accompanied by noise and degraded comfort. The very heavy curb weight combined with rear-axle steering also accelerates inside-edge tire wear when alignment drifts. These are wear/durability concerns rather than safety recalls but can be expensive once out of warranty.
before.solution: Have the suspension inspected for a leaking air strut, failing compressor/valve block, or worn sway-bar links/bushings when clunks or ride-height faults appear; address AIRMATIC malfunction messages promptly before a leak burns out the compressor. Replace failed rear shocks/dampers (often under warranty or service bulletin early on). Keep the car on an annual alignment to limit inside-edge tire wear from the heavy weight and rear-axle steering.

before.title: Battery Management System Software Overload Triggers High-Voltage Shutdown (NHTSA 24V372000)
before.description: On a large population of EQ vehicles, continuous diagnostic requests from other onboard control units can overload the battery management system's (BMS) memory capacity. This causes the BMS to open the high-voltage contactors, disconnecting the battery pack from the powertrain and producing a sudden loss of drive power. Mercedes-Benz USA recalled 14,912 EQE/EQS/EQE SUV/EQS SUV vehicles in June 2024 (NHTSA campaign 24V372000). Unlike many EQ software fixes, this remedy could not be delivered over the air and required a dealer visit, making it a recurring frustration for owners. The same BMS software is used on EU-spec cars.
before.solution: An authorized Mercedes-Benz dealer must reprogram the battery management system software; this cannot be done via OTA update. Owners should verify VIN against recall 24V372000 and schedule the dealer reflash. Until corrected, a high-voltage shutdown can occur with little warning, so prompt completion is advised.
symptoms: Vehicle shuts down / will not move

before.title: Electric Drivetrain Software Fault Causing Sudden Loss of Propulsion (NHTSA 23V405000)
before.description: A software error in the electric drivetrain's fault-management logic can deactivate the electric drive unit while driving, causing a sudden loss of drive power. Mercedes-Benz discovered the issue in October 2022 after a field report of an electrical drivetrain malfunction, and issued a U.S. recall (NHTSA campaign 23V405000) in July 2023 covering 8,281 vehicles. The fault-management software reacts incorrectly to drive-unit connector contact issues and shuts down propulsion as a precaution. This is a meaningful safety concern because power can be lost in traffic. EU-spec EQS vehicles run the same drivetrain software and were addressed in parallel manufacturer software recalls.
before.solution: Mercedes dealers reflash the electric drivetrain control software free of charge under the recall; no hardware replacement is typically required. Owners can check VIN against the recall at the NHTSA or Mercedes-Benz recall portals and have the update applied. If a loss-of-power event occurs, the vehicle should be brought in promptly for diagnosis and the latest drivetrain software.
symptoms: Sudden loss of drive power while driving

before.title: Flush/Retractable Door Handles Fail to Present, Locking Owners Out
before.description: The EQS uses electrically presenting flush door handles that pop out as the driver approaches. Owners widely report handles that fail to extend, require multiple pulls, or do not present at all, occasionally locking the owner out of the car. The handles are not heated and can freeze solid in winter, and forcing a frozen handle can damage the presentation motor. Some failures are software glitches (handle won't present on touch but works with the key fob), while others are mechanical/motor failures, with several owners reporting repeat handle replacements within months. This is a known issue across the keyless-go Mercedes range and is highly relevant in cold EU climates.
before.solution: If a handle won't present but the key fob still operates the door, the cause is usually software; a 12V battery disconnect/reset for ~15 minutes often restores function, and a dealer software update may be needed. For frozen handles, carefully de-ice rather than forcing them, and use the owner's-manual emergency unlock (mechanical key in the door) to avoid lockout. Mechanically failed handles or presentation motors are replaced individually; budget several hundred dollars per handle out of warranty.
symptoms: Requires multiple pulls to open door
Handle works with key fob but not on approach

before.title: MBUX Hyperscreen Freezing, Blackouts and Random Reboots
before.description: The 56-inch MBUX Hyperscreen and central display are a frequent complaint among EQS owners, who report lag, frozen screens, full blackouts and random reboots, especially on early 2022-2023 cars. A frozen Hyperscreen temporarily disables navigation, charge planning, climate control and the reversing/360 camera view, which is a real usability and safety annoyance. German owners on motor-talk.de have documented total MBUX failures mid-trip (e.g. a complete blackout during a Switzerland-Poland drive). Over-the-air updates frequently stall partway and sometimes require the car to sit at a dealer for a manual flash. Most cases are software rather than a hardware defect, though heat exposure and rare failing display hardware are also cited.
before.solution: Try a soft reset by holding the central display power/volume control, or perform a 12V battery disconnect for ~15 minutes to force a system restart. Keep MBUX software current; if an OTA update hangs, the dealer can cancel and re-push or manually flash the unit. Persistent blackouts that survive a reset warrant a dealer diagnosis for a possible display/head-unit hardware replacement (a four-figure part out of warranty).
symptoms: Loss of navigation and climate controls

before.title: Recurring 'Battery Malfunction / Do Not Tow' Warning and Front Motor Interlock Faults
before.description: Many EQS and EQS SUV owners report frequent 'Battery Malfunction' and 'Malfunction - Towing is not permitted' (Do Not Tow) dashboard messages, in some cases once or twice a month during the first 20,000 miles. The message appears to be a catch-all for several underlying conditions. In milder cases the car still drives and the warning self-clears or resolves with an ignition/12V reset; in severe cases the car refuses to shift into Drive, Neutral or Reverse and is immobilized. A subset of these events trace to a front electric motor 'interlock' fault that prevented the car from being put in Park and required Mercedes to replace the front electric drive motor under warranty. Owners frequently note multiple dealer visits and long parts waits before resolution.
before.solution: For a transient warning, switch the car off, wait ~5 minutes, then restart; if that fails, a 12V battery disconnect/reset often clears it. Persistent or shift-inhibiting faults require dealer diagnosis: many are resolved with battery/drivetrain software updates (often bundled with the BMS and drivetrain recalls), while a confirmed front-motor interlock fault requires replacement of the front electric drive unit under the EV powertrain warranty.
symptoms: 'Do Not Tow' / 'Towing is not permitted' message
Vehicle will not go into Park

before.title: 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain
before.description: The EQS experiences parasitic 12V battery drain when parked for extended periods, preventing the car from waking up or responding to the key fob. If the car will be parked for extended periods, use a 12V trickle charger connected to the auxiliary battery. Mercedes dealers can test for excessive parasitic draw from modules failing to enter sleep mode.
